cr_data.provenance: (An American Placce, New York, NY); David Hunter McAlpin, Princeton, New Jersey, 1942 (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive notes backing inscription and indicates, "inscription in ink in the margin 'This pastel is No. 14'." Title refers to Narcissa Swift (Mrs. Clinton) King, a friend of the artist. O'Keeffe and Narcissa Swift drove from Chicago to New Mexico in June 1940. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.notes: Source of title: Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks, 1941 New York (An American Place–O'Keeffe) exhibition checklist, backing inscription.
titles.title: Narcissa's Last Orchid

description: A large flower with white and pink petals dominates the composition. The flower's white petals have rippling, textured edges and contrast with a dark brown background.
imageCaption: Image courtesy of a scanned transparency made for Georgia O'Keeffe: Catalogue Raisonné. This image has not been color proofed and may differ from the original. It will be replaced when newer photography becomes available.
